stories.headline: Red Sea and Hormuz tensions keep pressure on global shipping and energy routes
stories.summary: Morning global feeds are dominated by Middle East escalation: Livemint reports Saudi oil tankers bound for China and India turned around after a Houthi threat in the Red Sea, while Al Jazeera is tracking U.S.-Iran tensions and warnings over any Iranian toll or restriction around Hormuz.
stories.pastoral_note: This is a moment to pray for peace beyond slogans: for leaders with restraint, for sailors and civilians caught in geopolitical crossfire, and for congregants anxious about how distant conflict becomes local cost-of-living pressure.

stories.headline: Nigeria remains a deadly pressure point for persecuted Christians
stories.summary: Open Doors' latest stories highlight a Nigeria food crisis driven by attacks, and its 2026 World Watch List material describes Nigeria as a global epicentre of deadly violence against Christians. A recent ICC-linked report also names Nigeria, Nicaragua, Syria and India among places where persecution pressures are rising.
stories.pastoral_note: Hold this before the church as family news, not merely foreign news. Hebrews 13:3 gives the frame: remember prisoners and the mistreated as though we were with them.

stories.headline: Gen Z still wants home, marriage and family—but feels the road narrowing
stories.summary: Ipsos' 2026 Generations work says traditional aspirations have not vanished: across 30 countries, 60% of under-35s still expect to own a home, 52% expect marriage and 48% expect parenthood. Yet Ipsos also notes economic pressure, milestone delay and a temptation toward 'live for today' pessimism.
stories.pastoral_note: This is fertile pastoral ground: many young adults are not rejecting covenantal life so much as wondering whether it is available to them. Preach hope as a concrete future, not vague optimism.

stories.headline: Tech companies turn to faith leaders for AI ethics conversations
stories.summary: AP reports that representatives from companies including Anthropic and OpenAI met with faith leaders at the inaugural Faith-AI Covenant roundtable in New York. The initiative aims to develop moral norms for rapidly advancing AI, with future gatherings expected in Beijing, Nairobi and Abu Dhabi.
stories.pastoral_note: The church should not outsource moral formation to technologists, but neither should it retreat. This is a timely opening to teach wisdom, human dignity and discernment in ordinary digital life.

stories.headline: HBR: Leaders must watch the hidden traps of team dynamics
stories.summary: Harvard Business Review's leadership page features '4 Hidden Traps of Team Dynamics,' arguing that leaders need awareness, humility and intention to navigate differences on their teams. Another highlighted piece warns that every organization has two realities: what leaders think they run and what employees actually experience.
stories.pastoral_note: For church leadership, this is a gentle diagnostic: culture is not what we announce, but what people experience. Healthy shepherding listens for the gap between stated values and lived reality.

stories.headline: Local housing conversation keeps circling first-time buyers and affordability
stories.summary: Fraser Valley Real Estate Board's NewsReal feed is currently highlighting CREA's campaign aimed directly at first-time buyers, while CREA continues to point Canadians to monthly resale data and the MLS Home Price Index, developed with boards including Fraser Valley and Greater Vancouver, as key tools for tracking price trends.
stories.pastoral_note: Housing is discipleship-adjacent in the Lower Mainland: it shapes marriage timelines, family formation, generosity, mobility and anxiety. It is worth praying for provision without turning home ownership into ultimate security.

stories.headline: El Salvador eliminates trachoma as a public health problem
stories.summary: Positive News reports that the WHO has recognized El Salvador for eliminating trachoma, the world's leading infectious cause of blindness, as a public health problem. The report notes a 94% global decrease since 2002 in the number of people at risk of trachoma.
stories.pastoral_note: This is a good reminder that quiet, sustained mercy works. The kingdom often advances through sanitation, medicine, community trust and faithful public health labour long before it becomes a headline.

stories.headline: Researchers say major AI models often omit religion from life's biggest questions
stories.summary: USA Today reports on CEFE-AI research from BYU, Notre Dame, Yeshiva and Baylor finding that major AI models often avoid religious perspectives when asked about grief, forgiveness, marriage strain, happiness and freedom—even while suggesting friends, parents or therapists.
stories.pastoral_note: Evangelistic edge: people are still asking ancient soul questions, even when they ask machines. The church can graciously say, 'You are not only a problem to solve; you are a person to shepherd toward God.'
